lines.japanese: 三階建てのマンション……ああ、これか。
lines.english: A three-story apartment building... Ah. This was it.

lines.japanese: ルーズリーフに書かれた地図とその建物を交互に確認した。間違いない。
lines.english: I compared the building with the map on the loose-leaf sheet. There could be no mistake.

lines.japanese: 一戸建てに住んでいる僕は、集合住宅にあがる機会が少ない。団地に住んでいたことはあるけど、子どもの頃だったからあやふやな記憶しか残ってない。
lines.english: Because I lived in a detached house, I rarely had occasion to enter an apartment building. I had lived in a housing complex once, but I had been a child then, and only hazy memories remained.

lines.japanese: エントランスはオートロックじゃなかった。見慣れない縦長の集合ポストで渡来さんの部屋番号を確認して、直接階段を上がっていった。
lines.english: There was no automatic lock at the entrance. I found Watarai’s apartment number on the unfamiliar vertical bank of mailboxes and went straight up the stairs.

lines.japanese: ドアの前に立つ。防犯のためか表札に名前は出てないけど、目印だっていう怪獣のシールがたしかに貼られてあった。
lines.english: I stood before the door. Perhaps for security, there was no name on the nameplate, but the monster sticker she had told me to look for was there.

lines.japanese: 僕は考える。インターホンを押したら渡来さんが出てくるだろう。
lines.english: I considered the situation. Once I pressed the intercom, Watarai would answer.

lines.japanese: その時に一番自然な挨拶はなんだろう。そうだ、ここでよくシミュレートしておいた方がいい。チャンスは一度しかないんだ。
lines.english: What would be the most natural greeting when she did? Yes—I ought to simulate this properly beforehand. I would have only one chance.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう！　今日は手伝ってくれてありがとう！」
lines.english: Good morning! Thank you for helping me today!

lines.japanese: ……駄目だ、変にテンションが高いと思われそうだし、だいたい僕のキャラじゃない。
lines.english: ...No. She would think I was strangely excited, and it was not remotely in character.

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます、わたくし渡来さんの級友で羽田と申しますが、明日香さんはご在宅でしょうか？」
lines.english: Good morning. My name is Haneda, a classmate of Miss Watarai’s. Might Asuka be at home?

lines.japanese: ……親はいないって言われてるのに、なんかわざとらしいかな。
lines.english: ...She had already told me her parents would be out. That sounded rather affected.

lines.japanese: 普通でいいんだ普通で。よし、普通を考えよう。
lines.english: Ordinary was fine. Ordinary. All right, think of something ordinary.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう。羽田です」
lines.english: Good morning. It’s Haneda.

lines.japanese: うん、このくらいが自然でいいんじゃないか。よし、これだ。
lines.english: Yes. That sounded natural enough. All right. This was it.

lines.japanese: 僕は頭の中で予行練習を繰りかえし、人差し指を水平に構えた。
lines.english: I rehearsed it over and over in my head, then leveled my index finger at the button.

lines.japanese: いくぞ……。
lines.english: Here goes...

lines.japanese: 「はーい」
lines.english: “Coming!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、渡来さん？　羽田だよ。おれ羽田鷹志」
lines.english: “Oh, Watarai? It’s Haneda. Me—Takashi Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあ目閉じて」
lines.english: “Oh. Then close your eyes.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　なに、目……？」
lines.english: “What? Why, my eyes...?”

lines.japanese: 「いま行くから」
lines.english: “I’m coming now.”

lines.japanese: 目を閉じてって言われても……とりあえず廊下を歩いて近づいてくる音が聞こえたので、慌てて言われた通りにした。
lines.english: Close my eyes...? Footsteps were already approaching along the hall, so I hurried to do as I had been told.

lines.japanese: 待つこと数秒、ドアが開く音に、室内の温かい空気。
lines.english: A few seconds passed. The door opened, and warm air flowed out from within.

lines.japanese: 「はいじゃあ上がって」
lines.english: “All right. Come on in.”

lines.japanese: え、上がってってこのまま？
lines.english: Come in? Like this?

lines.japanese: なんて戸惑っていたら、僕の右手になにか柔らかいものが触れた。
lines.english: While I hesitated, something soft touched my right hand.

lines.japanese: 温かい彼女の手が僕の手をぎゅっと包む。どきりとした。
lines.english: Her warm hand folded tightly around mine. My heart gave a leap.

lines.japanese: 「私の部屋以外は片付けてないから、まっすぐ付いてきてー」
lines.english: “I only cleaned my room, so follow me straight there.”

lines.japanese: ぐいぐい引っぱられる。
lines.english: She tugged me insistently onward.

lines.japanese: 「目開けたら殺すから」
lines.english: “Open your eyes and I’ll kill you.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “A-all right.”

lines.japanese: 彼女が物騒なことを言うから、靴も揃えられずに彼女の部屋までまっすぐ向かうことになった。
lines.english: Her alarming threat left me no chance even to straighten my shoes. I went directly to her room.

lines.japanese: 「はい、いらっしゃい」
lines.english: “There. Welcome.”

lines.japanese: 目を開いた。そこは初めて肉眼で見る、親族以外の女の子の部屋だった。
lines.english: I opened my eyes. For the first time in my life, I was seeing the bedroom of a girl outside my family.

lines.japanese: 緑を基調にしたフローリングの部屋。なんとなく女の子の部屋はピンクが基調っていうイメージを勝手に持っていたんだけど、この方が気持ちが落ちついていいなと思った。
lines.english: The room had wooden floors and was decorated mostly in green. For no particular reason I had imagined a girl’s room would be predominantly pink, but this felt calmer and more pleasant.

lines.japanese: 僕のイメージする女の子の部屋にはぬいぐるみや人形が置いてあるんだけど、もの自体が少なくて、なんていうか渡来さんらしい。
lines.english: In the girls’ rooms I had imagined, there were stuffed animals and dolls. Here there were very few possessions at all, which somehow seemed just like Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「はい、きょろきょろしない」
lines.english: “Hey. No gawking.”

lines.japanese: 「きょろきょろなんてしてないよ」
lines.english: “I’m not gawking.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと。興味なくても社交辞令でいいから明日香部屋を誉めようよ」
lines.english: “What was that? Even if it bores you, common courtesy says you should compliment Asuka’s room.”

lines.japanese: 興味がないわけじゃない。ただ僕は部屋よりも、その……渡来さんの私服姿に意識がいってるんだ。
lines.english: It was not that the room did not interest me. It was simply that my attention was fixed more on... Watarai in her everyday clothes.

lines.japanese: 一年生のとき、森里くんに服のショップに連れていってもらってから、僕も恰好にはそれなりに気を使うようになった。
lines.english: Ever since Morisato had taken me shopping for clothes in our first year, I too had paid a certain amount of attention to how I dressed.

lines.japanese: でも渡来さんはちょっとおしゃれに背伸びした程度の僕と違って、気を張ったところのない自然なファッションだ。
lines.english: But while I was still trying a little too hard to look stylish, Watarai dressed with an effortless naturalness.

lines.japanese: なんていうか、かっこいいひとは選ぶものから違うんだと認識させられる。
lines.english: It impressed upon me that stylish people differed from the rest of us even in what they chose.

lines.japanese: 「え、次の言葉が出ないほど酷かったんだ明日香部屋」
lines.english: “What? Asuka’s room is so awful it left you speechless?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええと、とってもかわいいと思うよ」
lines.english: “Um... I think it’s very cute.”

lines.japanese: 「かわいい。かわいい要素あるかこの部屋」
lines.english: “Cute? What part of this room is cute?”

lines.japanese: いつもの制服姿も非の打ち所がないけど、私服姿も嘆息するほどかわいい。
lines.english: She was flawless in her uniform, but in ordinary clothes she was lovely enough to draw a sigh.

lines.japanese: 「すごくいいと思う。うん、おれは渡来さんのセンス好きかな」
lines.english: “I think it’s wonderful. Yes. I like your taste, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、それは嬉しいなあ、ありがとう。あんまり物はないけどね」
lines.english: “Oh, that makes me happy. Thank you. There isn’t much here, though.”

lines.japanese: そんなことないよ渡来さん。まさか口に出しては言えないけど、出るとこ出てるっていうか、君はとてもいいスタイルをしていると思う。
lines.english: That was not true, Watarai. I could never have said it aloud, but where it counted she had plenty. She had a wonderful figure.

lines.japanese: 「なんだか初めて見るから新鮮だな」
lines.english: “It’s nice, seeing this for the first time.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、だって初めて連れてきたからね」
lines.english: “Well, yes. It’s the first time I’ve brought you here.”

lines.japanese: 「気にすることないのに。すごく細いからびっくりしたよ」
lines.english: “Nothing to worry about. I was surprised, honestly. So slim.”

lines.japanese: 「細い！？　えっ、細いってどこが？」
lines.english: “Slim? What’s slim?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは挙動不審に部屋の中を見回した。もしかしたら僕が失礼なことを言ったから、困ってるのかもしれない。話題を変えよう。
lines.english: Watarai darted anxious glances around the room. Perhaps I had said something rude and put her at a loss. I should change the subject.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり渡来さんみたいにいい物を選ぶと、高かったりするの？」
lines.english: “When you pick out nice things the way you do, do they tend to be expensive?”

lines.japanese: 「値段っ！？　や、いや、家賃かあ……多分、普通なんじゃないかなあ、相場通り」
lines.english: “The price?! N-no—oh, the rent... It’s probably normal. About the going rate.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、意外だなあ。でも、安くていいものがある店を見つけるのも、一つのセンスなんだろうね」
lines.english: “Really? That’s surprising. Finding things that are both good and inexpensive must be part of having taste.”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううーん……そうなの、かなあ……」
lines.english: “M-mmm... Maybe...?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはしばらく首を傾げたあと、ふらりと廊下の奥へと姿を消した。
lines.english: Watarai tilted her head for a while, then drifted away into the hall.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いまお茶淹れるから適当に座ってて」
lines.english: “Oh, I’ll make some tea. Sit wherever you like.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あ、ありがとう。でも、適当って？」
lines.english: “Thank you. But... wherever?”

lines.japanese: どうしよう、自分の部屋なら床に座るけど、それでいいのかな。それとも椅子に座った方がいいのかもしれない。
lines.english: What should I do? In my own room I would sit on the floor, but was that right here? Perhaps I ought to use the chair instead.

lines.japanese: そんなことを考えていたから、渡来さんが戻ってくるまで結局僕は立ったままだった。
lines.english: I remained absorbed in the question until Watarai returned and, in the end, was still standing.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ゴメン、クッションでも出せばよかったね。ええとじゃあ、この辺座ってもらっていいかな」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. I should’ve put out a cushion. Um... would you sit here?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、こっちこそゴメンね」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I’m sorry too.”

lines.japanese: 「いま作業用のテーブル用意するから、待っててね」
lines.english: “I’ll set up a table for the work. Just wait there.”

lines.japanese: 僕は窓側を背にして床に正座した。せめて片膝を立てればよかったと後悔したものの、今から足を崩すのはかっこ悪い気がしたから、そのままでいることにした。
lines.english: With my back to the window, I sat formally on my heels. I immediately regretted not leaving one knee raised, but changing position now seemed undignified, so I stayed as I was.

lines.japanese: あとで話の途中にでも体勢を変えよう……。
lines.english: I would shift naturally in the middle of the conversation later...

lines.japanese: 「ふう」
lines.english: “Haaah.”

lines.japanese: 作業の途中に体を伸ばしたら、渡来さんもちょうど手を休めたところだった。
lines.english: I paused to stretch, and Watarai had just stopped working too.

lines.japanese: 休憩にもなるし、さっきから気になってたことを聞いてみよう。
lines.english: It would make a good break, and I could ask about something that had been bothering me.

lines.japanese: 「そういえば……」
lines.english: “Come to think of it...”

lines.japanese: 「ん、なに？」
lines.english: “Hm? What?”

lines.japanese: 「この部屋って家族のひとはどこで過ごしてるの？」
lines.english: “Where does the rest of your family spend their time in this apartment?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、言ってなかったっけ。私、一人暮らしなんだよね」
lines.english: “Oh, haven’t I told you? I live alone.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ。そうなの？」
lines.english: “You do?”

lines.japanese: 知らなかった。ていうか渡来さんの私生活なんて考えたこともなかった。
lines.english: I had not known. In fact, it had never occurred to me to wonder about Watarai’s private life.

lines.japanese: 「一人で全部やるっていろいろと大変じゃない？」
lines.english: “Isn’t it hard, doing everything by yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ三年間も続けてるといい加減慣れるよ」
lines.english: “After three years, you get used to it whether you like it or not.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうものなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: そういえば渡来さんは料理が上手だ。一人暮らしをしてるうちに身についた技術かもしれない。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Watarai was an excellent cook. Perhaps it was a skill she had acquired from living alone.

lines.japanese: なんだか同い年なのにすごいなあ……じゃあ洗濯や掃除も一人でしてるってことか。
lines.english: It was impressive, considering we were the same age. So she did her laundry and cleaning by herself as well.

lines.japanese: なんでも叔母さんや小鳩に任せてる僕からすると耳の痛い話だ。
lines.english: For someone who left everything to his aunt and Kobato, this was painful to hear.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ友達とかお客さんが来たときも、渡来さんが一人で相手してるんだ。すごいね」
lines.english: “Then when friends or guests come over, you host them all by yourself. That’s impressive.”

lines.japanese: 「さっきは飲み物も用意してくれてありがとう。あ、でも、おれも途中でペットボトル買ってきたんだ」
lines.english: “And thank you for making me a drink earlier. Oh, but I bought a bottle on the way here too.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、差し入れ？　ありがと、じゃあグラスだけ持ってくる」
lines.english: “Oh, you brought drinks? Thanks. Then I’ll just bring glasses.”

lines.japanese: 「任せてよ、コップは自分のを用意しなくちゃと思って、途中で紙コップも買ってきたんだ」
lines.english: “Leave it to me. I thought I ought to bring my own cup, so I bought paper cups too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふ、ふーん……」
よかった、昨日の夜に買っていく物リストを作っておいたのが幸いしたみたいだ。クラスメイトの家に入るのは初めてだけど、今のところ順調に進んでいるじゃないか。
lines.english: Good. The list of things to bring that I had made last night was serving me well. This was my first visit to a classmate’s home, yet so far everything was proceeding without a hitch.

lines.japanese: 僕は紙コップを二つ取りだして、それぞれにこの前渡来さんが買ってきてくれたものと同じアップルソーダを注いだ。
lines.english: I took out two paper cups and poured us each the same apple soda Watarai had bought the other day.

lines.japanese: 「てゆかゴメンね。学校とか外なら平気なんだけど、自分の家だと気の使い方がよく分かんなくて」
lines.english: “I mean, sorry. I’m fine at school or when we’re out, but in my own home I don’t really know how you’re supposed to treat a guest.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなの？　どうして？」
lines.english: “Really? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、私自分の部屋とか、友達の部屋で遊んだことないから」
lines.english: “Mmm. I’ve never hung out with friends in my room—or in theirs.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「驚くとこじゃないよ。羽田君は私が友達少ないの知ってるじゃん」
lines.english: “That’s hardly shocking. You know I don’t have many friends, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは手に持っていたシャーペンをくるんと一回転させた。
lines.english: Watarai gave the mechanical pencil in her hand a single twirl.

lines.japanese: 「て、いうか……渡来さんの場合、友達だと思ってるひとが少ないだけで、逆に渡来さんを友達だと思ってるひとは多いと思うよ」
lines.english: “I mean... in your case, I think it’s only that you consider very few people friends. Plenty of people probably think of you as theirs.”

lines.japanese: 「うん知ってる」
lines.english: “I know.”

lines.japanese: 「でもそんな、一方通行の友人を部屋に呼んだりする？　やだよ私、自分の部屋が心を休められる最後の砦だもん」
lines.english: “But would you invite someone into your room when the friendship is all on their side? I wouldn’t. My room is my last refuge, the one place I can relax.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、そうかな……」
lines.english: “Is that so...?”

lines.japanese: 経験がない僕には分かりそうもない話だった。ん？　あれ、ということは……。
lines.english: It was not a subject I had enough experience to understand. Wait. In that case...

lines.japanese: 「おかわり」
lines.english: “More.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、好きに注いでいいよ。あ、ところでいまの話だと、じゃあ渡来さんの部屋に入ったのって……」
lines.english: “Help yourself. Oh, but from what you just said, the person who’s been in your room is...”

lines.japanese: 「おかわり」
lines.english: “More.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがコップを持った手を突きだしてきたので、二杯目のりんごジュースを注いだ。
lines.english: Watarai thrust out the hand holding her cup, so I poured her a second helping of apple soda.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、一人でなんでも出来るって言うんだったら、ジュースくらい自分で注ぎなよ……」
lines.english: “If you can do everything by yourself, you could at least pour your own drink...”

lines.japanese: 「ひとに注いでもらった方がおいしいよね」
lines.english: “It tastes better when somebody else pours it for you.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……どうなんだろう」
lines.english: “Does it...?”

lines.japanese: 無邪気にも見えるけど、逆らえないなと思わされる怖い笑顔だった。少なくとも男なら。
lines.english: Her smile looked innocent enough, but there was something frightening about it that made you feel you could never say no. Not if you were a man, anyway.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君も誰かに注がせてみれば分かるよ」
lines.english: “Have somebody pour for you sometime. Then you’ll understand.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、そんなの……」
lines.english: “No, thank you...”

lines.japanese: 「ふう」
lines.english: “Haaah.”

lines.japanese: りんごジュースを口につけて渡来さんが小さく息をつく。
lines.english: Watarai brought the apple soda to her lips and released a small breath.

lines.japanese: 「ま、初めてだよね」
lines.english: “Well... yes. You’re the first.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　うそだあ、渡来さんは色んなひとに注がせてるんじゃないの」
lines.english: “What? That can’t be true. I’m sure you’ve made all sorts of people pour drinks for you.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて、この部屋にひとが来るの」
lines.english: “That’s not what I mean. I mean you’re the first person who’s come into this room.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー……」
僕は自分のりんごジュースに口をつけながら、空気的な相槌を打った。
lines.english: I sipped my own apple soda and murmured something noncommittal to fill the silence.

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 俺が驚くのと同時に、机の上に紙の束が降ってきた。
lines.english: Just as I reacted in surprise, a sheaf of papers landed on the table.

lines.japanese: 「よし、作業やろう」
lines.english: “All right. Let’s get back to work.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっと待って……」
lines.english: “Wait a moment...”

lines.japanese: 僕は話の続きをしたくて、作業を止めようと腰を浮かした。
lines.english: I wanted to continue the conversation, so I started to rise, intending to halt the work and pick up where we had left off.

lines.japanese: 「あたっ」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、どしたの？」
lines.english: “What happened?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、大丈夫だよ、ちょっと足が……」
lines.english: “I’m fine. It’s just my legs...”

lines.japanese: 作業中ずっと正座してたから痺れたんだ。やっぱり片膝立てておけばよかった。
lines.english: I had spent the whole work session sitting on my heels, and my legs had gone numb. I should have raised one knee after all.

lines.japanese: 「あ、もしかして足痺れた？」
lines.english: “Oh, did your legs fall asleep?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで渡来さんは嬉しそうな顔してるの」
lines.english: “Why do you look so delighted?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、つつこうと思って」
lines.english: “I was thinking I’d poke them.”

lines.japanese: 「や、やめてよ。なにさらりと怖いこと言ってるの」
lines.english: “D-don’t! How can you say something so terrifying so casually?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが喜色満面の笑みでシャーペンを構えていた。
lines.english: Watarai leveled her mechanical pencil at me, beaming with delight.

lines.japanese: 「いただきます」
lines.english: “Time to dig in.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、挨拶の単語間違えてるよ。やめてよ」
lines.english: “That’s the wrong thing to say! Stop!”

lines.japanese: 「じょわっち」
lines.english: “Hi-yah!”

lines.japanese: 「やめっ、やめてよ渡来さん、やめてっ……あつうっ」
lines.english: “Stop—stop it, Watarai! Stop... Owww!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは満足してほっこりした表情を浮かべると、黙って作業に戻ってしまった。
lines.english: Wearing an expression of warm contentment, Watarai silently returned to work.

lines.japanese: 残念なことに僕の質問はそのまま有耶無耶にされてしまった。
lines.english: Regrettably, she had managed to leave my question unresolved.

lines.japanese: と言っても、渡来さんの部屋に入った男子一号としての栄誉が嬉しくて、残念でもなんともなかった。
lines.english: Then again, I was so delighted by the honor of being the first boy admitted to Watarai’s room that I did not regret it in the least.

lines.japanese: 「一息入れよっか」
lines.english: “Shall we take a break?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと二人で進めたら、思ったより早く作業は進んだ。
lines.english: Working together, Watarai and I had made faster progress than I expected.

lines.japanese: 月曜日までに終わらせるところは片付いた。これなら高内さんになにか言われることもないと思う。
lines.english: We had finished everything due by Monday. Now Takauchi should have no grounds for complaint.

lines.japanese: 僕が体勢を崩してリラックスすると、渡来さんはアルバム用に使う写真を見て楽しんでいた。
lines.english: I relaxed my posture while Watarai entertained herself with the photographs intended for the album.

lines.japanese: 「見てこれ、一年のころだよ。こうやってみると懐かしいねえ、これなんて完全に素の顔だよ私。うわすっご、超ブサイク」
lines.english: “Look at this—our first year. They feel nostalgic when you see them like this. This one caught my face completely unguarded. Oh wow. I’m hideous.”

lines.japanese: たぶん誰が見ても綺麗な横顔が写っていた。このワンショットを捉えたカメラマンを誉めてあげたい。
lines.english: The picture showed a profile that almost anyone would probably have called beautiful. I wanted to commend the photographer who had captured that instant.

lines.japanese: 「だから見ないでって」
lines.english: “I told you not to look.”

lines.japanese: その写真はすぐに没収された。本音を言うと欲しかったけど仕方ない。
lines.english: She confiscated the photograph at once. Truthfully, I wanted it, but there was nothing to be done.

lines.japanese: 僕は自分の持っている二年前の体育祭のワンショットまで没収されないように、携帯をポケットの中で握りしめた。
lines.english: I closed my hand around the phone in my pocket, lest she confiscate the snapshot from the sports festival two years ago that I had saved on it.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、テレビでもつけるね」
lines.english: “I’ll put the television on.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが脚を組みかえた拍子に、短いスカートがギリギリまで引っぱられた。
lines.english: When Watarai recrossed her legs, the hem of her short skirt drew taut almost to the limit.

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて目を逸らした。そうだ、せっかくつけたんだからテレビを見ればいい。画面の中にはマイクを持った女性が立っていた。
lines.english: I tore my eyes away. Yes—the television was on, so I ought to watch it. A woman holding a microphone stood on the screen.

lines.japanese: テレビの内容はどこにでもありそうな話題、とくに興味を惹かれる話題じゃないけど、僕は無理してでも意識を向けているように見せかける必要があった。
lines.english: The report was the sort of commonplace story one saw everywhere, nothing that interested me. Still, I needed to look as if I were paying attention, even if I had to force it.

lines.japanese: 「柳木原だって、怖いねえ」
lines.english: “They say it’s Yanagihara. Scary, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだね……」
lines.english: “Yes. Very...”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんから会話を投げかけられたけど、返事は適当になった。
lines.english: Watarai offered me the opening for a conversation, but my answer came out perfunctory.

lines.japanese: 女性キャスターが「怖いですねー」と言いながら画面が録画したものに切りかわる。画像の粗い赤外線カメラで撮影したような映像が映しだされた。
lines.english: The female presenter said, “It certainly is frightening,” and the screen cut to recorded footage, apparently shot by a grainy infrared camera.

lines.japanese: こういうのってやらせじゃないんだ。目にはモザイク、まるでこちらに気づく様子もない青年たち。
lines.english: So these things were not staged. The young men, their eyes pixelated, showed no sign that they had noticed the camera.

lines.japanese: 右下にありきたりのテロップが出てきた。「柳木原の夜に激増する少年犯罪」。
lines.english: A conventional caption appeared in the lower right: “Juvenile Crime Surges in Yanagihara After Dark.”
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、本当にほんの一瞬だった。
lines.english: It lasted an instant. Barely an instant.

lines.japanese: 興味のない画面の中、柳木原の歓楽街……昔、誰かがピンフ通りと呼んでいた場所で、髪の長い男の子がお尻を蹴られて笑っていた。
lines.english: There, inside the screen I had no interest in, was Yanagihara’s entertainment district—a place someone had once called Pinfu Street. A long-haired boy was laughing as somebody kicked him in the backside.

lines.japanese: その髪の長い男の子は僕のよく知っているひとに似ていた。まるで画面越しに声が聞こえてくるみたいだ。かかか。
lines.english: The long-haired boy resembled somebody I knew well. It was almost as though I could hear his voice through the screen. Ka-ka-ka.

lines.japanese: いつか一年生のときに森里君と買いにいったセレクトショップ。僕は彼が鏡の前でそれを合わせていたので、似合うよと誉めた記憶がある。
lines.english: I remembered the clothing boutique where Morisato and I had gone shopping in our first year. He had held that very garment against himself before the mirror, and I had told him it suited him.

lines.japanese: その服と同じものを映像の中の青年は着ていた。
lines.english: The young man in the footage was wearing the same clothes.

lines.japanese: 彼を蹴った足にも見覚えがある。足だけじゃない。側に置いてあるスポーツバック。いつもよりぼさぼさの後頭部。そして一瞬だけ振りむきかけた横顔。
lines.english: I recognized the foot that kicked him too. Not only the foot: the sports bag lying nearby, the back of a head more disheveled than usual, the profile that half turned for a single instant.

lines.japanese: 画面の中に興味はなかったのに、気づいたらそこに吸いこまれていた。
lines.english: The screen had held no interest for me, yet before I knew it, it had pulled me inside.

lines.japanese: あれは……あの顔は……。
lines.english: That was... That face was...

lines.japanese: ぼく？
lines.english: Me?

lines.japanese: 「なんでやねんっ！」
lines.english: “What the hell are you doing?!”

lines.japanese: 関西弁の男が、笑いながら相方にツッコミを入れた。リモコンを持った渡来さんが何かに迫られたような表情で僕の顔を見ている。
lines.english: A man speaking Kansai dialect laughed as he delivered the straight man’s retort to his comedy partner. Remote in hand, Watarai looked into my face as though something were closing in on her.

lines.japanese: その渡来さんに対して僕の顔は多分……笑ってたと思う。
lines.english: The face I showed Watarai in return was probably... smiling, I think.

lines.japanese: だって僕が森里君のお尻を蹴ってるなんてあるわけない。
lines.english: Because there was no possibility that I had been the one kicking Morisato in the backside.

lines.japanese: 他人の空似なんてことはよくあることだ。あれはなにかの間違いなんだ。
lines.english: Perfect strangers looked alike all the time. It had to be some sort of mistake.

lines.japanese: だって森里君は僕の友達なんだから。
lines.english: Because Morisato was my friend.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、そろそろ休憩終わりにしよっか」
lines.english: “Haneda, shall we get back to work?”

lines.japanese: テレビの切れる音が僕の意識を呼びさました。渡来さんがリモコンで電源を切ったんだろう。
lines.english: The sound of the television switching off roused me. Watarai must have pressed the button on the remote.

lines.japanese: 今度は意識をしながら笑顔を浮かべて僕は彼女に訊ねた。
lines.english: This time I deliberately arranged a smile on my face before asking her.

lines.japanese: 「いまの見た？」
lines.english: “Did you see that?”

lines.japanese: なにを言ってるんだろう。自分でもどうしてこんなことを訊ねたのか分からない。
lines.english: What was I saying? I did not understand why I had asked her that.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは唇を横に結びながら首を横に振った。
lines.english: Watarai pressed her lips into a line and shook her head.
“I didn’t...”

lines.japanese: 「てない」
lines.english: “...see it.”

lines.japanese: 「見てない？」
lines.english: “You didn’t?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとに？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「本当」
lines.english: “Really.”

lines.japanese: 「おれによく似たひとが見えたんだ」
lines.english: “I saw someone who looked just like me.”

lines.japanese: 「別人じゃない？」
lines.english: “Maybe it was somebody else?”

lines.japanese: 「そっか……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: しゃんしゃんしゃん　しゃんしゃんしゃん
lines.english: Jingle, jingle, jingle. Jingle, jingle, jingle.

lines.japanese: 大気から無数のきらめきが滲みでて、世界が金色に包まれていくのが分かった。
lines.english: Countless flecks of radiance seeped from the air, and I could tell that the world was being enveloped in gold.

lines.japanese: 「別人ってことは見てたんだ」
lines.english: “If you know it was somebody else, then you did see it.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりおれが映ってたんだ」
lines.english: “It really was me on the screen.”

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田君？　なに言ってるの、ちょっと落ちついて」
lines.english: “H-Haneda? What are you saying? Please, calm down.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんに、見られちゃった」
lines.english: “You saw me, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「待って、違うよ。きちんと話せば分かることだから、お願い、聞いて」
lines.english: “Wait, that isn’t it. We can clear this up if we talk it through. Please—listen to me.”

lines.japanese: 「恥ずかしいよ……」
lines.english: “I’m so ashamed...”

lines.japanese: 「わ、分かった、それなら私も聞きたいことあるから。だから耳ふさいで逃げたりしないでよ、ねっ？」
lines.english: “A-all right. Then there’s something I want to ask you too. So don’t cover your ears and run away, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら現実から目を逸らさないで、ちゃんと前を見ようよ」
lines.english: “Come on. Don’t turn away from reality. Look straight ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おれはそんな弱い人間じゃない……」
lines.english: “I-I’m not that weak...”

lines.japanese: 「でも現実にいま逃げてるじゃん」
lines.english: “But the fact is, you’re running away right now.”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ、羽田君？　はっ、羽田君！　はねだくーんっ……」
lines.english: “Huh? Haneda? H-Haneda! Hane-daaa...!”

lines.japanese: そして僕の意識は完全に途絶えた。
lines.english: And then my consciousness cut out completely.
